Clinical Information: 58-year-old female with a non-painful, pigmented lesion on the left cheek. The lesion has been present for approximately one year, with a recent slight increase in size. Clinical concern for atypical nevus vs. seborrheic keratosis.
Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled with the patient's name and "left cheek," is a single shave biopsy of skin measuring 0.5 x 0.4 x 0.2 cm. The specimen is a tan-brown, slightly verrucous papule. The deep margin is inked black. The specimen is bisected and submitted entirely in one cassette.
Microscopic Description: Microscopic examination reveals an exophytic proliferation of benign basaloid keratinocytes. The architecture shows prominent acanthosis, papillomatosis, and the formation of numerous keratin-filled invaginations and horn pseudocysts. The basaloid cells are uniform in appearance with small, regular nuclei and no significant mitotic activity or pleomorphism. Within the underlying dermis, there is a mild, patchy, perivascular infiltrate composed of lymphocytes and occasional eosinophils. The deep and peripheral margins are free of the lesion. No evidence of dysplasia or malignancy is identified.
Diagnosis: Skin, left cheek, shave biopsy: Seborrheic keratosis, irritated.
Comment: The histologic features are characteristic of an irritated seborrheic keratosis. The irritation corresponds to the mild dermal inflammation seen microscopically. Clinical correlation is recommended.
Specimen: One piece of skin from the left cheek, measuring 0.5 x 0.4 x 0.2 cm.

Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.

Diagnosis: Kidney, native, biopsy: Lupus Nephritis, Class IV-G (A)
Light Microscopy Description: The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to 28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. All glomeruli show global, diffuse endocapillary and mesangial hypercellularity with neutrophilic infiltration. Multiple glomeruli contain wire loop lesions. IgA: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.

C1q: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
Fibrinogen: Negative.
Albumin: Negative.
Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells. There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.
Comment: The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS 2003 Class IV-G (A).
Specimen: Native kidney biopsy

Date of Procedure: 06/20/2025 Date of Report: 06/25/2025
Clinical History: 28-year-old female with a one-month history of a painless, enlarging left-sided neck mass. Associated with night sweats. Concern for lymphoma. 
Diagnosis: Lymph Node, Left Cervical, Excision: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis Type. 
Gross Description: Received fresh, labeled 'left neck mass,' is an encapsulated lymph node measuring 2.8 x 2.1 x 1.5 cm. The cut surface is tan-white and firm, with a vaguely nodular appearance. Microscopic Description: Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal architecture by a nodular infiltrate. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis. Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammatory background composed of small lymphocytes, eosinophils, and histiocytes. Scattered throughout this background are large, atypical cells, including classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells have large, vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm. Immunohistochemistry: The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype: 
CD30: Positive 
CD15: Positive 
PAX5: Positive (dim) 
CD45: Negative 
CD20: Negative 
CD3: Highlights the background T-cell population. 
Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+, PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.
Specimen: Left cervical lymph node
Pathologist: Dr. Benjamin Ayers
Report status: Final

Clinical History: 45-year-old female with a 2.5 cm solid, hypoechoic nodule in the right lobe of the thyroid, discovered on ultrasound. 
Diagnosis: Thyroid, Right Lobe, Fine-Needle Aspiration: Suspicious for Malignancy (Bethesda Category V). 
Specimen Adequacy: The specimen is adequate for evaluation. 
Microscopic Description: The aspirate is cellular and shows crowded clusters of follicular cells with a microfollicular architecture. The cells exhibit nuclear enlargement, chromatin pallor, and irregular nuclear contours. Occasional nuclear grooves and rare intranuclear cytoplasmic pseudoinclusions are identified. Comment: The cytomorphologic features are suspicious for papillary thyroid carcinoma. Per the Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology, surgical excision is recommended for definitive diagnosis.

Clinical History: 56-year-old female with a new 1.2 cm cluster of pleomorphic microcalcifications in the left breast at the 10 o'clock position, identified on screening mammogram (BI-RADS 4C). 
Diagnosis: Left Breast, 10 o'clock, Core Biopsy: Ductal Carcinoma in Situ (DCIS), intermediate nuclear grade. 
Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled 'left breast cores,' are five tan-white, firm core biopsies, ranging from 1.2 cm to 1.5 cm in length. A specimen radiograph confirms the presence of microcalcifications corresponding to the area of concern. The cores are submitted entirely in one cassette. 
Microscopic Description: Sections show breast tissue with multiple ducts expanded and filled by a monotonous population of atypical epithelial cells. The architecture is predominantly solid and cribriform. The cells exhibit moderately enlarged, pleomorphic nuclei with irregular contours. Central necrosis (comedonecrosis) is present within some of the involved ducts, associated with psammomatous microcalcifications. No evidence of stromal invasion is identified in the tissue provided. 
Comment: The findings are diagnostic of Ductal Carcinoma in Situ. As this is a core biopsy diagnosis, definitive grading and assessment of margins will be performed on the subsequent excision specimen. Radiologic-pathologic correlation is recommended.
Specimen: Left breast core needle biopsy
Pathologist: Dr. Amanda Wright
Report status: Final
